To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a diet low in glycemic index and moderate in carbohydrate content has beneficial effects on glucose metabolism, insulin sensitivity, and hepatic fat content in healthy individuals during weight regain; and 2) the glycemic index of the diet is an important determinant of glycemic response and insulin sensitivity during weight regain.

a diet low in glycemic index and moderate in carbohydrate content (i.e. low glycemic load) may have health advantages by favorably impacting daylong glycemia and insulin sensitivity and by reducing liver fat.
a diet with moderate amounts of carbohydrate and low glycemic index (i.e., glycemic load) is associated with better glycemic control and liver fat during refeeding after calorie restriction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of diet quality and glycemic index on glucose and lipid regulation during weight regain after weight loss.
the impact of carbohydrate intake and glycemic load on metabolism during refeeding in healthy men after weight loss.
how the quantity and quality of dietary carbohydrates affects metabolism during refeeding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a high GI diet is not beneficial for glucose and lipid metabolism, but that the effect of GI on these parameters is not as strong as the effect of CHO intake.
a diet with a low GI and moderate amount of CHO intake (i.e., a low GL diet) has beneficial effects on daylong glycemia and liver fat, but not on IS, during refeeding in healthy men.
carbohydrate intake and quality affect glucose and lipid metabolic health during weight regain in men.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quality and quantity of CHO consumed during weight regain are important factors in maintaining health.
the glycemic index of carbohydrate (CHO), not total CHO intake, is an important determinant of glucose and lipid metabolism in healthy men.
the quality of carbohydrates, not just the quantity, is an important determinant for the regulation of glucose and lipid metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a low-GL diet may be beneficial for weight maintenance.
a diet that is low in GL may be beneficial to health.
the glycemic index and glycemic load of diets consumed during weight maintenance may be important determinants of metabolic health.
